sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.title: Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game
sources.text: GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive. "Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media . It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy. "Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted. Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure. For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot . But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag. Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page . Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

sources.text: Deciding whether to kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6 is the culmination of the Hey Arnold mission in Chapter 1, the 7th after you encounter Mandy during Pipework. Essentially, Arnold, Brian's business partner, has gone dark, so you're sent to rough him up. Arnold and his cronies will do a runner, hopping into a vehicle and speeding off. sources.title: Should you spare Arnold in GTA 6?
sources.text: Your choice to spare or kill Arnold in GTA 6 has consequences In the mission 'Hey Arnold!' you face the story's first major moral dilemma: do you kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6? After Brian's shady business associate, Arnold, goes dark during GTA 6 Chapter 1 , Jason, Brian, and Cal hunt him down to the radar station near the Aerostat. It turns out Arnold isn't very happy with Brian's drug-dealing tactics and, after some heated words, Arnold and his goons jump into a pickup truck and speed off. But no one disrespects Brian like that, not on Jason's watch, and a high speed car chase immediately ensues. When the chase ends, you must choose whether to let Arnold live or execute him, with your choice impacting your GTA 6 criminal profile . If you continue chasing Arnold to the Key Lento Marina, he abandons his vehicle and Brian tells Jason to "shut him up." Though, he doesn't specify how. He simply says: "Do whatever you have to do." You then need to chase after Arnold on foot (hopefully you've been working on your fitness) until you get close enough to tackle him or he reaches the end of the pier and has nowhere else to run. He then begins to beg Jason for his life. To spare Arnold, hold down L2/LT to interact with him and press X/A to select the option to 'Spare' him. Instead of killing Arnold, Jason will threaten him and let him go. In return, you receive a contribution toward the Restrained criminal profile and Arnold scuttles off, with Brian none the wiser. There are two ways you can kill Arnold in this GTA 6 mission . The first is to complete the car chase to the Marina and then follow Arnold on foot until he reaches the end of the pier or you're able tackle him to the ground. However, when he starts begging for his life, you can instead execute him with your weapon. If you do this, you receive a warning that "Indiscriminate violence will contribute toward a violent criminal profile." If you'd rather not deal with Arnold's begging – or a pesky foot chase – you can kill Arnold by shooting at his vehicle and/or him during the car chase. Killing Arnold in this way is quicker, but contributes toward a Ruthless criminal profile. Whichever choice you make, the following cutscene will be the same. sources.title: GTA 6 Shows Why You Should Never, Ever, Ever Text and Drive (Ever)
sources.text: If you need to check Snapmatic, pull over You can pull off a lot of heinous crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Stealing a car, mugging an old lady at gunpoint, killing a bird and then beating up a cop with its corpse. All of those are sure to earn you at least a one-star Wanted level. But there’s an even worse crime in GTA 6 that you’ll probably wind up doing more than murder: texting and driving. The most important tools that Jason and Lucia have in GTA 6 are their cell phones. Rockstar makes much of the game’s UI elements diegetic by cleverly cramming them into phone apps. People will text you mission locations to explain why quest markers are appearing on the map. A news app full of absurd stories will teach you Leonida lore without you needing to find scattered logs. You’ll even manage your workout routine through a fitness app. You can easily get distracted by your phone in-game, just as you would in real life. Rockstar Games deliberately plays into that with one of GTA 6 ’s most devious features. You can pull out your phone at any time and use it in first-person – and that includes while driving. Pick up your phone behind the wheel, and you’ll barely be able to see out your windshield as your focus is drawn to your glowing screen. It's one of the many small, but effective ways that GTA 6 lampoons everyday life in the 2020s. Considering that driving already requires care and attention, the task becomes even more difficult with a phone in one hand. You’ll find yourself swerving more erratically, and most assuredly getting into accidents. I have read-ended cars and run down pedestrians because I was too busy liking memes on Snapmatic. I’m not proud of that; scratched my damn car! What’s especially devilish about the system is that GTA 6 constantly tempts you to pick up your phone. Jason and Lucia will get text messages ad nauseam. Sometimes they’ll learn an important story detail, or get the location of a mission location they’ve been waiting for. Other times, Jason might just get a friendly text from Lucia asking what he’s up to. As an obsessive communicator, I always felt like I needed to respond right away or else I’d wind up leaving these people hanging. So anytime I’d get a text while driving, I’d look at the road, determine when I could look down for just a second, and then fire off a reply. And every time, I would wind up skidding over a bridge. You can argue, as many politicians and panicked parents have for decades, that GTA glorifies a lot of bad behavior. This, on the other hand, is probably the closest that the series has ever come to approaching a dangerous real-world act like a PSA. You absolutely should not text and drive in GTA 6 , just as you should not in real life. It doesn’t matter how quickly you can speed read a text; things happen quickly on the road. I mean, one time a drunk dude on a tractor cut me off out of nowhere! If you need to check Snapmatic, pull over to the side of the road and listen to some talk radio while you text. You wouldn’t want to mess up that paint job of the car you’re about to fence after stealing it from an old lady by beating her unconscious, right? Stay cool, follow the rules!

sources.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
sources.text: Or should you not trust the eccentric antiques dealer? Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive. Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. sources.title: Where is Dexter Morgan’s Apartment in GTA 6? Location Explained
sources.text: GTA 6 (and the series in general) is jam-packed with Easter Eggs and little nods to the real world. For fans of TV’s favorite serial killer, there’s a particularly cool location tucked away in Vice City. Dexter Morgan, the “protagonist” of Showtime’s long-running crime/thriller series Dexter , has a residence in the game since Vice City is a version of Miami, the city where the show takes place. No, you can’t actually go inside or find Dexter himself, but it’s still a fun road trip to go on if you’re in the know. Here’s how to locate Dexter’s apartment in GTA 6. You can purchase Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you still need a copy yourself. Dexter’s apartment is discoverable very early on in your GTA 6 journey. As soon as you’re through the Prologue and take control of Jason at his house, you’re able to access the correct location. Pop open your map and navigate over to Vice-Dale County. Thankfully, this is only one county away from your starting location of Mariana County. Vice-Dale County is just to the northeast. Even if you haven’t explored this section of the map, GTA 6 allows you to zoom in to undiscovered locations and see neighborhood names. You’re looking for Vice Beach, just east of Vice City itself. From here, zoom in further to Washington Island. You’re looking for the exact building shown in the map above, an angular structure with a swimming pool on the north side. Set a waypoint on your map, pick some good radio tunes, and make the trip. From Jason’s house, it’ll take you five or six minutes to reach via the freeway. Once you arrive at the location, you’ll notice a symbol on the side of the building, which is also a nod to Dexter. These are the Trinity Apartments, a reference to the Trinity Killer from season four of the show (the best one). Dexter’s apartment is on the second floor, so take any of the staircases around the building, the most obvious of which is the large, spiral staircase. The correct apartment is a corner unit on the second floor, very close to the body of water to the west. It’s the most northwestern unit on the second floor of the Trinity Apartments. Unfortunately, you can’t actually go inside the apartment, but it’s still a fun Easter Egg to discover. In addition to the “Trinity” reference already made, it seems the roof of the building also hides a nod to Dexter. Climb the ladder on the side of the building to access the roof, and walk over just next to the top of the spiral staircase. Here, you’ll see a particularly suspicious set of tools. A syringe, knife, rope, handcuffs, and other Dexter-related items are set out on the floor. You’re getting sloppy, Dex. You can claim the knife for yourself, as well as pocket a cool $68 from the orange toolbox. What’s your favorite Easter Egg in GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.text: When you start exploring Kelly County in Grand Theft Auto 6, most likely when you enter Chapter Two of this incredible open-world epic, you might stumble upon something otherworldly. I was exploring Kelly County after hitting Chapter Two in GTA 6, and I came across man at night standing on the hood of his car down a dirt road. sources.title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
sources.text: The PS5 triggers are changing how I drive in GTA. Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me. But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6 . GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff. Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point. I've been calling this low-speed mode . At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode. Don't worry, it's not hard to fully gun it either: Just pull the trigger with a little gusto and you're off to the races. This is what the two speeds look like: This has completely changed how I drive in GTA. I'm already someone who takes these games slowly, but the natural stopping point of the throttle makes this easy and natural—as if Rockstar is not just allowing for a more immersive playstyle, but endorsing it. It's just a different experience than having to manually learn the speed thresholds and intuitively hold the trigger at an exact middle point. This is more like I'm pulling the trigger to one natural stop for "slow", and another for "fast". It's the four-wheeled equivalent of Jason and Lucia's walk (you have to press L3 to enter a jog or sprint), or the default saunter of Red Dead Redemption 2's horses. I can only recall one other open world game with a similar feature: the older Mafia games had speed limit toggles that automatically prevented cars from surpassing the speed limit. I always liked that, too, but this is more elegant. It turns out Rockstar's co-branding campaign that insists GTA 6 "plays best on PS5" isn't just marketing. In these months before GTA 6 is a PC game , I really would suggest you play it on a PlayStation for the controller perks alone. And when the time comes, I hope Rockstar goes the extra mile to port these DualSense features to the PC version. sources.title: GTA 6 VP: "25 years on, the DNA remains" from Rockstar's original Vice City to modern Leonida
sources.text: Vice City has changed a lot over the years - but maybe less than you think With GTA 6 now so tantalizingly close that it's in the hands of players willing and able to pull off the New Zealand trick , it's very easy to get caught up in the now. After a 13-year wait for GTA 6, it can be easy to forget that all of the other GTA games were made over the span of just 12 years . But that's not what happened at Rockstar, as Stuart Petri, VP of art for 2D/UI design lays out - instead, he says that GTA 6 was the result of an uninterrrupted, 25-year process. In Rockstar's development notes, shared with press ahead of the GTA 6 review drop, Petri notes that "almost 25 years ago, we helped bring Vice City to life." That first foray to Rockstar's take on Florida "began as a simple visual design language," but has since "evolved into something far more sophisticated, layered, and considered." As Rockstar returns to Vice City for the first time since 2006's Vice City Stories, Petri notes that "we're returning to a world that has grown enormously in detail, creativity, and gameplay complexity." That meant that the series' art had to change too, ensuring it was relevant to a modern audience while "retaining the heritage that makes it unmistakably GTA." Petri discusses plenty about the discipline of UI art, but it's the underlying message about the history of Grand Theft Auto and the wider GTA identity that I think is most interesting. This series feels like such a known quantity, but it's really not - the world has changed an awful lot since 2013, and that's before we even touch on the differences in the gaming industry. Rockstar is releasing this game into a landscape that's wildly different to the one they last launched a Grand Theft Auto game into, but that doesn't seem to have phased Petri at all. In his part of the game, he says, "it's about building on that heritage" that the series thrives on, "and creating something that feels both entirely new and, at the same time, unmistakably GTA." He finishes by saying that "25 years on, the DNA remains," tying the very first version of Vice City to the one that we're all about to experience. sources.text: Infinity Nikki , the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates . Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother. Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car" , which doesn't actually fly. While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family. "If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer ). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear." "If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread . "Please please please be wrong." Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained. "She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY." Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content". "A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added. So far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players. In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review , Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020."

sources.title: Infinity Nikki Players Are Planning To ‘Girl-cott’ The Game Over Maye Musk Ad
sources.text: Infold Games, developers of Love and Deepspace and Infinity Nikki, are 0 for 2 in pissing off their international fanbase for both games. Earlier this year, the studio announced, then cancelled, Love and Deepspace ‘s sixth love interest, the werewolf Valko, inspiring some players to go on a sustained boycott that seems to have had a noticeable impact on the gacha game’s revenue in the months since. Now some Infinity Nikki players are hoping to achieve a similar effect, planning a “girl-cott” after Chinese ads for the dress-up gacha game featured Maye Musk , mom of noted racist and transphobe Elon Musk. Beyond the practical discussions of how exactly to inform Infold Games of player dissatisfaction, girl-cott conversations on the Infinity Nikki subreddit have devolved into thorny back-and-forths on where to draw the line about the thing you enjoy. Some players can’t play the game in good conscience, knowing that Infold Games would choose to partner with the mother of guy who said he fed the USAID organization, responsible for providing food and medical assistance to countries in need, “into the woodchipper,” an act projected to result in widespread death, infection, and suffering for millions, including children . Others don’t see the issue because Maye Musk is not her son, however odious he may be, and the antipathy for him seems to be a uniquely American sentiment with little bearing in the wider, international (and Chinese) Infinity Nikki community. As a player of both Infinity Nikki and Love and Deepspace , it’s interesting to see both communities arrive at the same fracture point in their relationships with their respective games over two very different events. It’s too early to tell how much of an impact the girl-cott will have, but its timing will no doubt hamper the momentum of the game’s upcoming 3.0 release later this month. sources.title: GTA 6 launch week revenue predicted to top the biggest movies from Star Wars, Harry Potter, and LOTR
sources.text: And it seems like a pretty good bet after becoming the most pre-ordered game on Sony and Microsoft's digital stores At long last, GTA 6 is finally here, and wouldn't you believe it – not only is it rather good, but it's also pretty popular. That wasn't unexpected, of course, and if one market intelligence and analyst firm's launch-week prediction proves accurate, Rockstar could be on track to earn more than the biggest Star Wars, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter movies combined. This is an observation highlighted by Gearbox boss Randy Pitchford, who writes on Twitter : "Newzoo's forecast is that GTA VI will generate more in its launch week than the entire original theatrical runs of the most successful Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars movies combined." He appears to be citing Newzoo's July estimate , following the game's pre-orders going live. At the time, it was predicted that GTA 6 could earn between $3.3 billion and $5.2 billion in total sales by the end of its launch week. Rockstar hasn't released any official data yet, but it's clear that GTA 6 is off to an exceptional start. Before launch, Sony and Microsoft confirmed that it was the most pre-ordered game of all time on their respective digital stores , and market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates that , as of yesterday, it had sold 17.07 million units and brought in $1.65 billion in revenue. So, how does that compare to the movies Pitchford highlights? Per Box Office Mojo, the single most successful movies (by lifetime box office revenue) from each franchise are Star Wars: The Force Awakens , The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King , and Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2 . The worldwide lifetime gross revenue for each of those comes in at around $2.07 billion, $1.12 billion, and $1.34 billion, respectively, for a combined total of about $4.53 billion. If Sensor Tower's most recent estimate is correct, then GTA 6 hasn't reached this high just yet, but we're only just on launch day – Newzoo was allowing for the full week in its previous forecast. And, if the analytics firm ends up being correct, then it could be on track to earn over half a billion dollars more than those movies in its first days, which is wild. With 10/10 GTA 6 reviews almost across the board, though, it's a deserved result for Rockstar. We'll just have to wait and see how high that number can go. sources.text: Rockstar co-founder issues rare public statement as the firm's latest release launches worldwide Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement as GTA 6 launches, celebrating the game's debut and its glowing critical reception . "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us," said Houser in a statement shared with IGN . "This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities – and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. "We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you. The game is currently available to players in New Zealand and Australia, and will unlock at midnight on the 19th in other territories. The review embargo lifted this morning, with the game receiving near-universal critical acclaim and setting record viewership figures on YouTube and Twitch .
